When MIGraphX is available and the model fits within its operator coverage — MIGraphX provides superior throughput via graph compilation

MIGraphX provides graph-level compilation (analogous to TensorRT for NVIDIA) for maximum throughput on AMD Instinct. ROCm EP is a generic fallback that executes operators individually without whole-graph optimization. When MIGraphX encounters unsupported operators, it automatically falls back to ROCMExecutionProvider or CPUExecutionProvider for those specific ops.

Use CPU EP only as a last resort. When both OpenVINO and oneDNN are detected, OpenVINO should be ranked higher in recommendations.

QNN (standard plugin) uses a multi-pass workflow: OnnxConversion → quantization → QNN compilation. This gives maximum control but more complexity. QNN ABI (QairtPipeline) compiles the model directly to a context binary in one pass — simpler workflow, preferred for fresh greenfield projects targeting Snapdragon 8 Gen 2/3+. The ABI path is newer (olive-ai 0.13.0+) and provides a more streamlined deployment experience.

Static quantization requires a representative calibration dataset matched to the inference distribution and yields better compression. Dynamic quantization computes scale/zp at runtime, needs no calibration, but can be slower and less accurate for CNNs.

Per-channel weights improve accuracy for CNNs but are slower and not supported on all mobile NPUs. Qualcomm NPU requires symmetric per-channel quantization. NVIDIA TensorRT supports per-channel but engine build is slower.
Symmetric quantization (zero point = 0) is easier for accelerators. Asymmetric can improve accuracy but requires hardware support and may fail on some NPUs. QNN/CoreML prefer symmetric.
Too few samples produce poor statistics; too many slow calibration with diminishing returns. A good starting point is 100-300 samples. Data must match inference distribution.
ONNX export with fixed batch/sequence dimensions creates inflexible models. Use dynamic_axes to preserve variable dimensions, especially for LLMs.
Higher opsets support more operators but reduce hardware compatibility. QNN and CoreML often require opset 13-17. Default to 14 unless a specific EP demands higher.
Models with weights >2GB must set use_external_data_format=True, producing a .onnx file plus .onnx_data external tensors. Failure to do so causes ONNX export OOM or invalid model errors.
Some frameworks default to float64 for small constants. ONNX Runtime and most EPs prefer float32. Cast constants before export or use OnnxFloatToFloat16 carefully.

Quantization passes (OnnxQuantization, QNNQuantization) require an ONNX input. Running quantization before OnnxConversion fails with a format mismatch. The canonical chain is Convert -> Optimize -> Quantize -> (Optionally) Float16.
Running OnnxFloatToFloat16 before INT8 quantization destroys the quantized graph. Apply FP16 after quantization only if you want a pure FP16 model, not a quantized one.
Running OnnxModelOptimizer or OrtTransformersOptimization before quantization produces a cleaner graph and often improves quantized accuracy by fusing LayerNorm/Attention patterns.

LoRA keeps the base model weights frozen and trains only low-rank adapter matrices. This means the base model can be quantized separately, but merging adapters into a quantized base model is non-trivial.
Rank 8-16 works for simple tasks; 32-64 for domain adaptation; 128+ for large distribution shifts. Higher rank increases train memory and adapter size.

QLoRA uses a 4-bit base model for training. After training, export the adapter and merge with a non-quantized base before ONNX conversion if you need ONNX. Merging adapters into a 4-bit base is not supported by Olive.

If an operator is not implemented for the requested EP, ONNX Runtime may silently fall back to CPUExecutionProvider, causing unexpected latency. Check EP-specific operator support and enable verbose logging.
QNN only supports a subset of ONNX ops. LayerNorm, GELU, and some gather/reshape patterns may need replacement or partitioning. Use QNNPreprocess when available.

Consumer TensorRT RTX path needs both the tensorrt-rtx package and a matching ONNX Runtime EP-ABI plugin build, not the full nvinfer TensorRT SDK. Missing install or SM < 7.5 leaves NvTensorRTRTXExecutionProvider unregistered.

Install both tensorrt-rtx and the matching ONNX Runtime EP-ABI plugin (Hardware → Install TensorRT RTX, or pip in the app venv). Requires NVIDIA GPU SM ≥ 7.5 (Turing+). Verify NvTensorRTRTXExecutionProvider appears in onnxruntime.get_available_providers(). Prefer AWQ INT4 (NVModelOpt) over PTQ INT8/QDQ for this EP. Restart the app after install.
DirectML execution provider missing or wrong venv
DirectML requires Windows 10/11 + DirectX 12 and onnxruntime-directml in the default-family venv. CUDA/GPU ORT wheels do not expose DmlExecutionProvider.

On Windows, install onnxruntime-directml into the Olive Studio default venv (Hardware → DirectML or pip). Do not mix CUDA/TRT packages into the DirectML EP path. Non-Windows hosts cannot run DirectML.
WebGPU is browser-only — local Execute Live blocked
WebGpuExecutionProvider targets ONNX Runtime Web in the browser. Olive Studio marks WebGPU recipes non-runnable locally (isRunnable: false / localExecutionIssues).
Use Export recipe / download ONNX for in-browser ORT Web WebGPU. Prefer FP16 (OnnxFloatToFloat16). Do not expect Execute Live or local Olive CLI to run WebGPU.
OpenVINO NPU needs target device NPU (not EP rename)
Intel NPU still uses OpenVINOExecutionProvider. The device is selected separately via openvinoTargetDevice (or equivalent). Without device=NPU and the OpenVINO NPU driver, work stays on CPU.

In Olive Studio set OpenVINO target device to NPU. Install the OpenVINO NPU driver on Intel Core Ultra / Meteor Lake+. Prefer OpenVINO weight-compression or INT8 paths; verify unsupported ops are not silently falling back to CPU.
RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device
Input shapes or dynamic_axes are not correctly specified; or the model contains control flow that depends on runtime shape.
Add dynamic_axes to OnnxConversion for batch/sequence dims; trace with representative input shapes; replace data-dependent control flow with fixed-shape equivalents.
ONNX protobuf cannot store tensors larger than 2GB.
Enable use_external_data_format=True; Olive will write weights to a separate .onnx_data file.
Calibration data is not representative, per-channel quantization is disabled for CNNs, or asymmetric scheme is used on an accelerator that requires symmetric.
Use 100-300 representative samples; enable per_channel=True for CNN/Linear layers; switch to symmetric quantization for QNN/CoreML; evaluate with a held-out set.
Execution provider silent fallback to CPU
The requested execution provider does not implement one or more operators; ONNX Runtime falls back to CPU.
Check EP operator support; add OnnxModelOptimizer to fuse unsupported patterns; consider OnnxOpVersionConversion to a supported opset; enable verbose ORT logging.
Out of memory during quantization or tuning
Calibration batch or intermediate tensors exceed GPU memory.
Reduce calibration_sampling_size and batch_size; move to CPU for calibration; use weight-only quantization; enable external data format for large models.
Static quantization requires a DataConfig with calibration samples that match the model input format and preprocessing.
Define a data_config with correct input_names, batching, and preprocessing; use representative samples from the inference distribution.
target_modules do not match the model architecture (e.g. using q_proj/v_proj for a BERT model).
Inspect model keys and set target_modules correctly: Llama/Mistral use q_proj/k_proj/v_proj/o_proj; BERT uses query/key/value/dense.
TensorRT engine build is very slow or fails
INT8 TensorRT requires per-engine calibration and explicit QDQ placement; dynamic shapes enlarge the search space.
Use static shapes where possible; pre-generate calibration cache; enable OnnxStaticQuantization with QDQ format before TensorRT; reuse engine files.
AWQ calibration is slow or hangs
AWQ scans weights and activations; large models or large calibration sets take time.
Reduce calibration iters to 32; use a small subset (128 samples); ensure GPU memory is available.
Qualcomm QNN has a limited op whitelist; LayerNorm and GELU are often unsupported.
Run QNNPreprocess before QNNQuantization; use OnnxModelOptimizer to fuse LayerNorm; consider replacing GELU with approximate ops if the model allows.
CoreML conversion fails with dynamic shapes
CoreML prefers fixed input shapes; dynamic batch or sequence length can fail.
Fix input shapes by removing dynamic_axes in OnnxConversion; use symbolic shape inference carefully.
LoRA adapter cannot be merged into quantized base
Merging adapters into a 4-bit or quantized base model is not supported by Olive.
Merge LoRA weights into the full-precision base model before ONNX conversion; then quantize the merged ONNX model.
OpenVINO silently falls back to CPU EP
OpenVINO Execution Provider does not support some ops or data types.
Check OpenVINO operator support; use OnnxModelOptimizer to fuse unsupported patterns; convert to OpenVINO IR for broader op support.
Transformer optimization fails due to missing dims
OrtTransformersOptimization needs num_heads and hidden_size for attention fusion.
Set num_heads and hidden_size in pass params; verify against model config.
INT4 quantization causes large perplexity increase
INT4 weight quantization is aggressive; small models or sensitive layers suffer.
Use group size 128 or 64; exclude lm_head and embedding layers from quantization; try AWQ or GPTQ with larger group size.
Model activations exceed FP16 range or are not trained for FP16.
Keep I/O types float32; cast int inputs to int32; exclude sensitive ops from FP16; consider mixed precision.
Calibration samples do not match inference inputs; quantization scale/zp are wrong.
Use production-like data; cover min/max sequence lengths and vocabulary; avoid synthetic or unrelated samples.
Pass output names collide or cache_dir is shared across runs.
Set unique output_name per pass; use separate cache_dir per experiment; clean cache between unrelated runs.
Objective weights or search space are not tuned; evaluator is noisy with small sample size.
Fix seed for reproducibility; use larger calibration/evaluation sets; adjust objective weights; try bayesian or evolutionary search.
TorchScript export fails for a HuggingFace model
Many HF models use control flow or data-dependent shapes that TorchScript cannot trace.
Use OnnxConversion instead of TorchScript export; configure dynamic_axes for variable dimensions.
Olive Python package not installed in the active environment
The process running the recipe cannot import olive (wrong venv or missing pip install).
Activate the Olive Studio / project .venv and pip install olive-ai (or the Olive extras your recipe needs). Re-run Execute Live from the app so it uses that interpreter.
ONNX Runtime CUDA EP missing from Python environment
CPU-only onnxruntime is installed, or GPU EP was not built into the wheel.
Install onnxruntime-gpu matching your CUDA tag in the same venv Olive uses. Confirm with python -c "import onnxruntime as ort; print(ort.get_available_providers())".
Hugging Face Hub authentication or gated model failure
Model is gated/private or HF token is missing/invalid in the Olive process environment.
Run huggingface-cli login or set HF_TOKEN for the Olive Studio server process. Accept the model license on huggingface.co, then retry.
Model path does not exist on disk
input_model.config.model_path points to a missing local file/folder or an unresolved HF cache path.
Verify the local path in Olive Studio Input, or switch to a Hugging Face id that can be downloaded. Clear stale relative paths.
Disk full during Olive export or cache write
ONNX external data, cache_dir, or Hugging Face downloads filled the volume.
Free disk space; point cache_dir to a larger volume; enable use_external_data_format only when needed and clean old experiment caches.
CUDA / cuDNN driver mismatch for Olive GPU run
Installed CUDA wheels expect a newer driver or cuDNN libraries are missing from PATH.
Upgrade the NVIDIA driver, match Olive Studio CUDA tag (cu121/cu124/…) to the wheel set, or fall back to CPUExecutionProvider for a smoke test.

Install a CUDA-capable bitsandbytes wheel for your platform, or disable QLoRA and use full-precision LoRA / GPTQ-AWQ paths that do not need BNB.
Triton dependency missing for an Olive GPU pass
Some quant/optim kernels import triton; Windows or CPU-only envs often lack it.
Install triton where supported, switch to a pass that does not require it, or run calibration on a Linux CUDA machine.
TLS/SSL failure downloading models or Olive assets
Corporate proxy, custom CA, or broken cert store blocks huggingface.co / azure downloads.
Configure REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / SSL_CERT_FILE for the Olive process, or pre-download models on a machine with working TLS and point model_path at the local folder.
Olive pass config failed schema validation
Recipe pass params do not match the installed Olive version (renamed/removed keys).
Compare pass params with Olive docs for your version; remove unknown keys; rebuild from Olive Studio UI defaults then re-apply advanced overrides carefully.
CUDA error: all CUDA-capable devices are busy
GPU device busy or unavailable to Olive
Another process holds the GPU, or CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES hides all devices.
Stop competing GPU jobs; check CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES; retry with a smaller calibration batch or CPU fallback for conversion-only steps.
DirectML execution provider not available to Olive
Olive/ORT process lacks onnxruntime-directml, or the host is not Windows with DirectX 12.
On Windows install onnxruntime-directml into the Olive environment; select DmlExecutionProvider. Do not expect DirectML on Linux/macOS or from CUDA-only ORT wheels.
WebGPU is not a server-side ONNX Runtime EP for Olive CLI
WebGpuExecutionProvider is for ONNX Runtime Web in browsers. Desktop/server Olive runs do not execute WebGPU the same way.
Build/export an ONNX recipe (prefer FP16) for browser ORT Web. For local Olive execution pick CUDA, TensorRT, DirectML, OpenVINO, or CPU instead.

HuggingFace model fails to load after upgrading to olive-ai 0.13.0

Olive 0.13.0 changed the default value of trust_remote_code from true to false for security. Models with custom code (e.g., Phi, Mistral with custom RoPE, Qwen) now refuse to load unless explicitly opted in.

In Olive Studio, open the Hugging Face source settings and enable Trust Remote Code. Enabling this executes Python from the model repository inside the Olive process on your machine, so only enable it for repositories you trust. Do not use Apply Fix for this setting; it must be toggled manually.
QairtPreparation or QairtGenAIBuilder pass not found in olive-ai 0.13.0
The QairtPreparation and QairtGenAIBuilder passes were superseded by the unified QairtPipeline pass in olive-ai 0.13.0. Recipes referencing the old pass names will fail.
Replace QairtPreparation and QairtGenAIBuilder with a single QairtPipeline pass. QairtPipeline combines model loading, quantization, and compilation into one YAML-recipe-driven step.
